# better-hermes-lcm v1.1.0-beta.2

A follow-up to `v1.1.0-beta.1` with one behavioural addition and a large comment cleanup.
Everything the first beta's notes say still applies — read those for what the fork is and what
it does not yet prove.

## The summariser's reasoning effort is now settable

`LCM_SUMMARY_REASONING_EFFORT` — `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`,
`ultra`. Empty by default, which sends nothing and behaves exactly as `beta.1` did.

The host's auxiliary client has accepted a per-call reasoning config all along; the plugin never
passed one, so a reasoning summariser always ran at whatever its route defaulted to and an
operator had no way to say otherwise. On this plugin that is not a tuning detail. The summary
*is* the index: a shallow pass over a 40,000-token chunk produces a list of topics, while a
deeper one names the decisions, rejected alternatives, identifiers, paths and outcomes that make
a leaf worth expanding — which is the whole premise of `lcm_expand`.

The level goes out as `extra_body.reasoning`, which covers both wires the host may end up on, and
the host clamps it per route: an unsupported level degrades to the nearest weaker one rather than
failing the call. The plugin stays provider-neutral and never needs to know what a route supports.

## The `# fork:` marker is gone from 578 comments

The reason for each hook stays exactly where it was; only the label went. It never was the
authoritative answer to "which lines are ours" — `git diff $(cat .upstream-base)..HEAD` is, it is
exact, and it cannot drift. This is the same argument that retired the hand-maintained
touchpoints table, applied one step further.

No behaviour changed: all 211 Python files parse, the plugin imports, and both anchors are clean.

## Verification

```
python3 scripts/e2e_no_loss.py 262144 400      → 0 unreachable rows, 0 missing facts, 0 never offered
python3 scripts/e2e_no_loss.py 1000000 3000    → 0 unreachable rows, 0 missing facts, 0 never offered
```

Still a beta, and still never run in a real session. The weighting remains frozen outside
256k–1M, and condensation is still verified by reading rather than by running.

## Install

```bash
git clone --branch v1.1.0-beta.2 --depth 1 \
  https://github.com/ConstantinLevin/better-hermes-lcm ~/.hermes/plugins/hermes-lcm
```
